A_target.statement: The [[Definition:3-Satisfiability Problem|3-SAT]] problem, of deciding satisfiability of [[Definition:Conjunctive Normal Form|CNF]] formulas with at most three literals per clause, is [[Definition:NP-Complete|NP-complete]].

B_source.statement:
The [[Definition:Boolean Satisfiability Problem|satisfiability problem]] for CNF formulas is NP-complete.
This is the [[Cook-Levin Theorem]].

substitutions.a long clause: a chain of three-literal clauses linked by fresh variables

object_map.reformulation: Split each long clause into a chain of short clauses with fresh linking variables, preserving satisfiability.

validity_conditions: Fresh variables must be distinct for each split clause.
The transformation is linear in the size of the formula; 3-SAT is in NP since assignments can be checked quickly.
proof_plan:
Replace each clause $l_1 \lor \cdots \lor l_k$ with $k > 3$ by:
:$\paren {l_1 \lor l_2 \lor y_1} \land \paren {\neg y_1 \lor l_3 \lor y_2} \land \cdots \land \paren {\neg y_{k - 3} \lor l_{k - 1} \lor l_k}$
with fresh variables $y_1, \ldots, y_{k - 3}$.
If some $l_j$ is true, set $y_i$ true for $i < j - 1$ and false for $i \ge j - 1$; every new clause is satisfied.

If every $l_j$ is false, the first clause forces $y_1$, then $y_2$, and so on, and the last clause fails.
Hence the new formula is satisfiable {{iff}} the old one is.
